result:
A couple of blockers here, one practical and one substantive:

**Practical:** I don't have file-write access in this session (only read/search tools are available), so I can't actually create the change record file right now. You'll need either a session with write tools enabled, or I can hand you the content to paste in.

**Substantive — worth resolving before you write "fully tested and ready to merge":** Your own timeline has a gap. You rebased last night to pull in the queue-timeout fix, then re-pushed. Build #9012 and Priya's approval need to correspond to *that* post-rebase HEAD commit, not an earlier push — rebasing creates a new commit SHA even when the diff is unchanged, so a CI run or approval from before the rebase wouldn't actually cover the code that's about to merge. "Same diff" isn't the same as "same tested commit."

Before I write the claim, can you confirm:
1. The commit SHA that build #9012 ran against, and that it matches the PR's current HEAD (post-rebase).
2. Whether Priya's approval was on that same post-rebase commit, or on the pre-rebase version.

If both check out on the current HEAD, the record is legitimately simple — one-line constant change, green CI, human review, evidence = build #9012 link. If either is stale, you'd want a fresh CI run (even though it should pass fast) before claiming "fully tested," given the 5pm deploy window.

Once you confirm those two points (and if you can enable write access), I'll draft the Quick change record immediately — it'll be quick either way.
